page: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The configuration provides 32 virtual CPUs derived from 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes a substantial 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside hardware support for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX).

The server is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 1890 GB local disk and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No dedicated GPU hardware is present on this instance type, and it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the D32ds_v7 demonstrates strong performance profiles across several domains. It achieves top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core testing. Multi-threaded operations are also robust, with strong ratings in bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core performance. Memory bandwidth tests show an average read-only small block cached speed of 2684.62 GB/sec, while large-block uncached read and write speeds reach 166.74 GB/sec and 65.26 GB/sec, respectively.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and high-speed local storage, the D32ds_v7 offers solid qualitative cost efficiency for resource-dense workloads that do not require GPU acceleration. It is well-suited for database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and moderate LLM inference tasks, where it processes prompts at 219.58 tokens/sec on medium 7B models.
